summary: A flux-tunable transmon with an Al/AlO$_x$/4Hb-TaS$_2$ Josephson junction was realized by sequential deposition and full in-situ oxidation of Al layers on exfoliated 4Hb-TaS$_2$, embedded in a 3D copper cavity, and characterized via two-tone spectroscopy and time-domain measurements. The device exhibits SQUID-like tunability and sub-microsecond $T_1$ (0.08–0.69 µs across devices), but exhibits rapid dephasing ($T_2^* < 16$ ns), and shows a factor-of-five deviation from the Ambegaokar–Baratoff relation, suggesting nontrivial junction physics in the hybrid system.
motivation: Van der Waals superconductors like 4Hb-TaS$_2$ offer unconventional order parameters, potential topological boundary modes, and subgap excitations inaccessible in conventional Al/AlO$_x$/Al transmons. Integrating them into circuit-QED requires a repeatable, robust junction process compatible with standard transmon fabrication.
method: A hybrid Al/AlO$_x$/4Hb-TaS$_2$ SQUID transmon was fabricated by sequential thin-Al deposition with full in-situ oxidation on exfoliated 4Hb-TaS$_2$ flakes, forming a controlled tunnel barrier, then capped with 200 nm Al. Two device geometries were tested: Design 1 routes supercurrent through the flake; Design 2 uses an asymmetric SQUID with one hybrid and one conventional junction to suppress bulk pathways.
result: Extracted parameters for device 1A: $E_C/h \approx 140$ MHz, $E_{J,\Sigma}/h \approx 11.6$ GHz, $d \approx 0.35$, $\omega_{01}/2\pi \approx 3.46$ GHz. Energy relaxation ranged $T_1 = 0.08$–$0.69$ µs; Ramsey dephasing timescale $< 16$ ns. Room-temperature junction resistances (1.9–2.4 kΩ) imply via Ambegaokar–Baratoff a gap of only 33–35 µeV, inconsistent with Al (162 µeV) and 4Hb-TaS$_2$ (390 µeV), suggesting suppressed Josephson coupling from anisotropic pairing or interface effects.
